lede: The biggest thing on the docket this week is Carhenge — the proposed redevelopment at 700 W. Pacific Avenue gets two separate hearings on September 30: HARC takes up the preliminary architecture review for the full building cluster, while a special Town Council session hears an appeal of the P&Z-approved lot subdivision that has to hold before any of it moves forward. Alongside that, the Gondola Leadership Committee weighs a genuinely consequential delivery choice on federal-versus-local project control, the County commissioners dig into a proposed Employee Housing Impact Fee, and the Town kicks off its 2027 budget work sessions.

notable.stake: Committee votes on federal vs. local control for gondola project delivery.
HARC reviews three preliminary large-scale applications for Carhenge redevelopment buildings.
Council hears appeal that could block or advance the Carhenge lot consolidation entirely.
Commissioners discuss proposed Employee Housing Impact Fee for unincorporated county.
Final architecture review vote on 15 employee apartments and 4 new multifamily units.
2027 General and Capital Fund priorities take shape before formal adoption begins.
